If make a claim to insurance for vehicle damage, the insurance company will get an estimate on how much it will cost to repair your vehicle to a "reasonable standard" or something like that (it will say in your policy) and will cut you a check for that amount. THIS CHECK HAS NO STRINGS ATTACHED! It is your money, and you can use it for whatever you wish. You can keep the money, and never repair the car. You can have the car repaired at a lower price, at a different body shop, or by doing some work yourself, or by asking the shop the use cheaper parts, etc. You can have some parts of the car repaired and leave others broken. Many people are under the mistaken impression that this is fraud. IT IS NOT. It is only fraud if you lie about the damage, or if you collude with the repair shop to get an artificially inflated estimate. I just went through this with an $8000 repair on my car. I ended up negotiating a lower price with the body shop, so I did not have to pay my deductible of $500. I verified with my insurance company, with the body shop, and with some online research after a bunch of people told me what I did was illegal. They were wrong. Save yourself some money by knowing how the process works!
